subject.title: Telegram: allow native channel commands in explicitly allowed chats

question: For Telegram channel_post commands, should OpenClaw fail closed unless an explicit channel policy authorizes both the chat and callback/session path, or intentionally allow explicit-chat-only semantics that ignore sender-scoped identity on this Telegram surface?
rationale: This PR changes a command execution surface where Telegram channel posts may lack the normal human sender, and the paired open issue shows the security semantics are not fully decided.

options.title: Fix Auth And Callback Semantics
options.body: Require explicit channel authorization, sender_chat-aware allowlist behavior, channel-aware callback/session routing, and live proof before merge.

options.title: Pause For Policy Resolution
options.body: Keep this PR open but blocked until the paired channel_post authorization issue settles sender-scoped allowFrom semantics.

options.title: Accept Explicit Chat Only
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally accept explicit-chat-only channel semantics, but should document the security rationale and prove allowed/denied live behavior.

recommendation.title: Fix Auth And Callback Semantics
recommendation.body: Require explicit channel authorization, sender_chat-aware allowlist behavior, channel-aware callback/session routing, and live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent history on the shared command-gating and Telegram group-access code that define this auth boundary.
